title: HavenLink - Connecting Families to Licensed Adoption Agencies
content: HavenLink - Connecting Families to Licensed Adoption Agencies A civic technology platform for adoption Every thread leads a child home. HavenLink gives prospective adoptive families one place to learn, prepare, and connect with licensed agencies. Start with the home study → See how it works Scroll Licensed agencies only No direct child contact Secure by design Spend less time on paperwork. Put more attention on connection. HavenLink organizes the early adoption process in one place. Families can learn what is required, complete an intake, and work with licensed agencies. 01Secure & structured matching 02Licensed agency verification 03Family-centered design 87% of families report confusion when navigating adoption agencies Adoption information is spread across agency sites, forms, and local requirements. Families often struggle to compare agencies and understand what comes next. HavenLink brings the core steps together and keeps licensed agencies involved throughout the process. HavenLink organizes the process into four steps. How It Works Four simple steps to connect families with their perfect match 01 02 03 04 01 Step 01 Home Study Service A comprehensive assessment by a licensed social worker evaluates your home, background, finances, and readiness to adopt, ensuring a safe and supportive environment for a child. 02 Step 02 Family Intake Form Complete a secure, guided intake form to share your family profile, preferences, and support needs. 03 Step 03 Compatibility Matching Our algorithm intelligently matches families with children based on preferences, needs, and fit. 04 Step 04 Agency-Managed Profiles Verified agencies post and manage child profiles with full transparency and structured information. Ready when you are Review the first step → Child safety shapes the entire platform. 01 No direct family-to-child contact Every interaction flows through verified, licensed agencies. Families never contact children directly. 02 Licensed agencies only Every partner agency is vetted, licensed, and accountable before a single profile is posted. 03 Secure accounts & encrypted data Guarded pages, session-secured authentication, and encrypted transport protect every record. 04 Privacy-first by design Minimal data collection and a transparent privacy policy govern the entire platform. Take the next step for your family. Start your home study → Are you an agency? title: The HavenLink Team - Meet Our Founders
content: The HavenLink Team - Meet Our Founders The people behind HavenLink № 01 — The Team The team building adoption's connective tissue. Meet the founders, licensed agencies, and civic partners responsible for building and supporting HavenLink. Meet the founders → Trace our global reach Scroll Founders 03 Licensed agencies 07 Civic partners 07 Countries 07 No child should wait because the adults around them couldn't find one another. HavenLink exists to close the distance between families, licensed agencies, and the institutions that safeguard children — one accountable network instead of a thousand disconnected phone calls. See how the platform works 01 № 01 Asad Sadikov Co-Founder · Data & Matching Asad Sadikov is a Co-Founder and lead technologist at HavenLink with strong expertise in data analysis, machine learning, and scalable system design. content: Home Study Service - HavenLink HavenLink Registry — Home Study Service Form HL-01 The assessment that opens the door. A home study is a licensed provider's written evaluation of your family's readiness to adopt, and every state requires one. The essentials never change: interviews, a home visit, background checks, and a report. The specifics belong to your state. Check your readiness → What a home study is Scroll Required in all 50 states The same essentials everywhere Two-minute readiness check What a home study is 01 - 03 One requirement, written fifty ways - the heart of it never changes. A home study is the written evaluation of your household that every state requires before an adoption can move forward. It exists to rule families in, not out. 01 Interviews with you and everyone in your household 02 At least one visit to your home 03 Background checks for every adult 04 Personal references who can vouch for you 05 A written report that travels with you Who conducts the study, what it costs, how long it takes, and whether training is required are all set by your state and agency. One conversation with a state-authorized provider settles all four. i. Application & interviews You apply, then talk through your story - your household, your history, your hopes. ii. The home visit Your evaluator sees where a child would live, sleep, and grow. iii. Checks & references Background checks for every adult, and a few people who can speak for you. iv. The written report Everything becomes the document that carries your family to the next step. The readiness check 02 - 03 Where are you on the path? If your home study is done, we'll take three details and move you straight to Step 2. If not, a short check shows where you stand and how to prepare. Which state was your home study completed in? Select a state… Please select a state to continue. Which agency or provider conducted your home study? The licensed agency, social worker, or organization that completed your study. Please enter the agency or provider name to continue. When was your home study completed? Most states consider a home study current for 12-24 months, so the completion date matters. Month Month… Year Year… Please select the month and year to continue. You're ready for the next step! Since your home study is already complete, you can move straight to Step 2: the Family Intake Form. We've sent your home study details to HavenLink so the team has them on file. Your home study may need an update It was completed more than 24 months ago, and most states require updates every 12-24 months. Your agency can tell you whether a renewal is needed. Continue to Family Intake Form → Before we get started, which state do you currently live in? Home study requirements differ by state, so we'll tailor the rest of the questions to where you live. Select your state… Please select your state to continue. Yes No Please select an answer to continue. A few items still need attention Here's what you can do next → For families living outside the United States Home studies for international residents must be conducted through a USCIS-accredited agency in your country of residence. Please visit uscis.gov/adoption for guidance. Great news - you appear to meet the basic requirements! Based on your answers, you appear to meet the basic eligibility requirements for a home study in [State]. We've sent your results to HavenLink - one of our partners will reach out at your account email to walk you through next steps and help schedule your consultation. In the meantime, the preparation resources below will help you get ready for the interview, the paperwork, and the home visit. We couldn't load the screening questions Something went wrong while loading your state's requirements. Please check your connection and try again. Preparation resources 03 - 03 What follows is the common ground across states. Your state or agency may ask for more - confirm the final list with the provider conducting your study. 01 Interview Preparation The home study interview is a guided conversation. Your evaluator's goal is to understand your family and readiness to adopt. The primary applicant(s) and all adults in the home are interviewed, and sometimes older children too. Common topics across all states Why you want to adopt and what led you to this decision Your upbringing and family background Your parenting philosophy and approach to discipline Relationship history (for couples: how you communicate and handle conflict) Your support system - friends, family, community What age range or background of child you're open to How you plan to support a child's cultural or racial identity (if adopting transracially) Your understanding of trauma, loss, and attachment Tips for answering well Be honest - evaluators are trained to recognize rehearsed answers You don't need to be perfect; you need to show you're self-aware and prepared It's okay to say "we're still learning about that" Disagreeing with your partner on some things is fine and normal What NOT to worry about A small home, modest income, or imperfect past does not automatically disqualify you. The process is designed to rule families in, not out. After the interview The professional conducting your study writes up their report, and you may be asked to address specific items. Approval timelines vary by state and agency, and commonly take several weeks to a few months. 02 Documentation Checklist This checklist covers documents required in most states. Your state or agency may require additional items - check with the provider conducting your study for a complete list. Your progress is saved on this device. Identity & Legal Valid government-issued photo ID - all adults in household Birth certificate - all household members Social Security card - all adults Marriage certificate (if married) Divorce decree(s) (if previously married) Proof of legal name change (if applicable) Financial Federal tax returns - most recent 2 years Pay stubs or proof of income - most recent 3 months Bank statements - most recent 3 months General summary of assets (home, vehicles, investments) General summary of debts (mortgage, loans) Proof of health insurance coverage Medical Completed physical exam for all adults (within the past 12 months) Physician statement confirming physical and mental fitness to parent Immunization records for all household members Mental health clearance (if requested by agency) Background & Legal Clearance State-level criminal background check - all adults (specific agency varies by state) FBI fingerprint-based background check - check if required in your state State child abuse registry clearance (required in most states) Home Proof of homeownership or current lease Homeowner's or renter's insurance Pet vaccination records (if applicable) References 3-5 personal reference letters (non-relatives preferred) - number varies by state and agency Reference contact information (name, relationship, phone, email) Additional (varies by agency or state) Vehicle registration and insurance Life insurance policy documentation (if applicable) Military discharge papers DD-214 (if veteran) Pre-adoption training certificate (required in some states) Autobiographical statement (required by many agencies) 03 Prepare Your Home During the home visit, the professional conducting your study confirms in person that your home is safe and has adequate space. Home safety standards are similar across most states, though some states have stricter rules for items like pools. Your progress is saved on this device. Throughout the home Working smoke detector on every floor - batteries tested Working carbon monoxide detector on every floor Fire extinguisher accessible (one per floor recommended) Emergency exit plan visible or discussed Unused electrical outlets covered with safety caps No exposed wiring or broken outlets Kitchen Cleaning products stored in a locked cabinet or out of reach Knives stored safely (drawer or knife block, not loose on countertops) Medications not stored in the kitchen Bathrooms All medications locked away or out of reach Water heater set to 120°F or below to prevent scalding Toilet locks if infant or toddler placement is anticipated Bedrooms Child's designated sleeping area identified - appropriate bed or crib No couch, hallway floor, or shared adult bed as the primary sleeping arrangement Window guards installed if above ground floor (for young children) Garage / Storage / Outdoors Chemicals, paints, and fuels in a locked cabinet or shed Tools stored safely Pool or hot tub fenced with a self-latching gate (California: must meet CA Swimming Pool Safety Act) Firearms unloaded, in a locked safe, with ammunition stored separately Tips for the visit itself Cleanliness matters but perfection doesn't - a clean, organized home demonstrates care Offer a walkthrough proactively; don't wait for your evaluator to ask Be present and relaxed - the visit is a conversation, not an inspection If you spot something that needs fixing, fix it before the visit rather than explaining it away After the visit Your evaluator writes their findings into a report. If any items need attention, you'll be notified and given time to address them before final approval. content: Family Intake Form - HavenLink Before you begin Notes for the applicant 01 Answer as the household you are — not the one you think an agency wants to read about. 02 Every answer saves to this device as you type. Leave and return whenever you like. 03 When you file, the dossier is sent to HavenLink and tied to your account. Nothing is published. Contents I Household Profile 0/8 II Lifestyle & Values 0/6 III Experience & Background 0/5 IV Adoption Preferences 0/8 V Legal Readiness 0/6 0% of the dossier complete No. 1 How many adults (18+) will be living in the home? required Please enter the number of adults (1–10). Include yourself and any other adults aged 18 or older. No. 2 What is the relationship between household adults? required Single adult Married couple Domestic partners Co-parents (unmarried) Other Please select a relationship type. No. 3 Do you currently have children living in your home? Yes No No. 4 How many children, and what are their ages? Children now at home An age for each child helps agencies think carefully about fit between siblings. No. 5 What type of home do you live in? required Single-family house Townhouse Apartment / Condo Mobile home Other Please select a home type. There is no wrong answer here — agencies care about stability, not square footage. No. 6 Do you own or rent your home? Own Rent Other arrangement No. 7 How many bedrooms are available for an adopted child? Shared room available 1 private room 2+ rooms available No. 8 What state do you reside in? required Select a state… Please select your state of residence. Your state drives agency routing and legal jurisdiction — the one entry we can never skip. No. 9 What is your approximate combined household income? Under $30,000 $30k – $50k $50k – $75k $75k – $100k $100k+ Prefer not to say Used only to surface assistance programs — never to screen a family out. § No. 10 How would you describe your household's activity level? Very active / outdoorsy Moderately active Relaxed / home-oriented Varies No. 11 Do you have a religious affiliation? Yes (optional to specify) No Spiritual but not religious Prefer not to say What is your affiliation? (optional) Optional, and used only for cultural matching when you want it considered. No. 12 Are you open to a child of a different cultural or ethnic background than your own? Yes, fully open Prefer same background Open with support resources Unsure No. 13 Do you have pets in the home? Yes No What types of pets? (select all that apply) Dogs Cats Birds Other Some children have allergies or fears — agencies simply like to know. No. 14 Describe your typical weekday structure. Both parents work full-time One works / one stays home Work from home Retired / flexible schedule No. 15 What languages are spoken in your home? (select all that apply) English Spanish Other Which other language(s)? Multilingual homes are a gift — children who share your language surface first. § No. 16 Have you previously fostered or adopted a child? Yes, foster care Yes, adoption Yes, both No No. 17 How many placements have you had, and what age ranges? Placements Infant (0–1) Toddler (2–4) School age (5–9) Preteen (10–12) Teen (13–17) Experienced families are often shown a wider range of matches. No. 18 Do you have professional childcare experience? Teacher / educator Social worker Therapist / counselor Healthcare (pediatric) None Other No. 19 Have any adults in the home completed adoption or foster training? Yes, PRIDE or equivalent Yes, other training In progress No No. 20 Has your household ever had a Child Protective Services (CPS) report? Yes No Thank you for your honesty We know this can be difficult to answer. A past report does not disqualify your family — it only routes your dossier to an agency with the right review process, and it stays confidential. In a few words, please share what happened.required Please add a brief note — a sentence or two is enough. Seen only by your assigned agency representative. Never public. No. 21 Do you have references available (non-family)? Yes, 2 or more Yes, 1 Working on it No § No. 22 What age range of child are you hoping to adopt? (select all that apply) required Infant (0–1) Toddler (2–4) School age (5–9) Preteen (10–12) Teen (13–17) Open to any age Please select at least one age range. Select every band you are open to — “any age” covers all of them. No. 23 Are you open to adopting siblings together? Yes, open to any group size Yes, up to 2 siblings Prefer single child Unsure Keeping siblings together is one of the kindest things a family can offer. No. 24 Do you have a preference for the child's gender? No preference Boy Girl Non-binary / open No. 25 Are you open to a child with a diagnosed medical condition? (select all that apply) No medical needs preferred Minor / manageable conditions Moderate ongoing needs Significant medical needs Open to any No. 26 Are you open to a child with a behavioral or developmental diagnosis? (select all that apply) No behavioral needs preferred ADHD / attention needs Anxiety / mood disorders Developmental delays Autism spectrum Trauma history (PTSD) Open to any Openness here changes what support we help you line up — it is never a test. No. 27 Do you have access to therapeutic or specialized support services in your area? required Yes, actively connected Yes, could access if needed Limited access in our area Unsure Because of the support needs you selected above, please tell us about your access to services. Registry note — support services You indicated openness to higher support needs with limited local access. Many specialized services are available remotely. Find a child & family therapist near you Registry note — trauma-informed care Children with a trauma history thrive with caregivers connected to trauma-informed support, including remote options: National Child Traumatic Stress Network Trauma & PTSD therapist directory May become required, depending on the needs you selected above. No. 28 Are you open to a child with a history of trauma or abuse? Yes, we have training / experience Yes, willing to learn Prefer not Unsure A note about teens in care Many teenagers awaiting adoption have experienced trauma. We recommend a conversation with an agency counselor before finalizing this preference — it does not affect your eligibility, and you can continue either way. No. 29 Are you open to maintaining contact with the birth family? Yes, open adoption Yes, occasional contact Prefer closed adoption Open to agency guidance § No. 30 What state will the adoption take place in? required Select a state… Please select the state where the adoption will take place. Both states must approve the placement before a child can move — routine, but it typically adds a few weeks. Your agency will guide the review. Learn more about the ICPC Pre-filled from your residence. Families sometimes adopt through another state — that is routine. A written assessment by a licensed social worker confirming your home is a safe, stable place for a child — interviews, background checks, a home visit, and references.
